req.title: Delete post
req.statement: The system shall remove the post row and redirect to / when POST /<id>/delete is issued by the post's author.

doc.reasoning: The delete post requirement has three key behaviours to verify: (1) a logged-in author can delete their own post and is redirected to / with the row removed from the DB; (2) a non-author (or unauthenticated) user cannot delete another user's post; (3) deleting a non-existent post returns 404. I also test the exact redirect Location header, the exact HTTP status codes (302, 403, 404), and verify the DB row is truly gone after deletion. Tests use only pre-loaded data: post 2 belongs to user Rahul (id=1, password='stone'), post 7 belongs to user Anjali (id=2, password='cloud').

tests.name: test_delete_own_post_redirects_and_removes_row
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
Post id=2 exists with author_id=1 (Rahul)
User Rahul (id=1, password='stone') is logged in
expected: Subsequent GET / does not contain post title 'Pillow delta willow'
Direct DB query confirms post id=2 no longer exists
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login as Rahul (author of post 2)
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302

# Delete post 2 (owned by Rahul)
r = client.post('/2/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

# Verify redirect target renders without the deleted post
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'Pillow delta willow' not in r.data

# Verify row is gone from DB
with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 2').fetchone()
    assert row is None

tests.name: test_delete_last_post_of_author_row_gone_index_empty_of_it
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
Post id=17 exists with author_id=3 (Ishaan)
Ishaan (id=3, password='stone') has exactly one post in the DB
expected: Post id=17 no longer exists in the database
No posts by Ishaan remain in the database
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Confirm Ishaan has exactly 1 post before deletion
with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    count_before = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post WHERE author_id = 3').fetchone()[0]
    assert count_before == 1

# Login as Ishaan (author of post 17)
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302

# Delete post 17
r = client.post('/17/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

# Verify post 17 is gone and Ishaan has zero posts
with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 17').fetchone()
    assert row is None
    count_after = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post WHERE author_id = 3').fetchone()[0]
    assert count_after == 0

tests.name: test_delete_post_state_transition_post_exists_then_absent
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
Post id=20 exists with author_id=1 (Rahul)
Rahul (id=1, password='stone') is logged in
actions: Confirm post 20 is absent via GET /
expected: Before delete: GET / returns 200 and contains 'Heacon signal pulse'
After delete: GET / returns 200 and does NOT contain 'Heacon signal pulse'
DB row for id=20 is absent
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# State 1: post exists
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data

# Login as Rahul
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r.status_code == 302

# Transition: delete post 20
r = client.post('/20/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

# State 2: post absent
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' not in r.data

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute('SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 20').fetchone()
    assert row is None
